target_moa.text: The mixture of proteolytic enzymes in NEXOBRID dissolves burn wound eschar; the effect is mediated by proteolytic activity that selectively debrides the eschar or denatured collagen. The specific components responsible have not been identified.

citations.quote: The mixture of enzymes in NEXOBRID dissolves burn wound eschar. The specific components responsible for this effect have not been identified.

Mechanism of Action	The effects of NexoBrid's active pharmaceutical ingredient is mediated by the proteolytic activity of the mixture of enzymes that selectively debride the eschar or denatured collagen.

modality.text: Enzyme (mixture of proteolytic enzymes extracted from the stems of pineapple plants, composed mainly of stem bromelain, ananain and other proteins; a botanical/biologic drug product for topical use).

citations.quote: The drug substance in NEXOBRID, anacaulase-bcdb, is a mixture of proteolytic enzymes extracted from the stems of pineapple plants (*Ananas comosus* [L.] Merr.) that has been sterile filtered and lyophilized.
The drug substance, anacaulase-bcdb, is composed mainly (80% to 95% w/w) of the proteins: stem bromelain, ananain, jacinin-like lectin, bromelain inhibitors, and phytocystatin inhibitor;

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were pruritus and pyrexia. In the integrated safety analysis (NEXOBRID N=177 vs SOC N=149): pruritus 15% vs 13%, pyrexia 12% vs 9%, wound complication 9% vs 6.0%, anemia 6% vs 5%. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis have been reported with postmarketing use.

basis.text: The Complete Response was issued due to numerous product quality (PQ) and Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) deficiencies, including significant unblinding/GCP issues in Study MW2010-03-02 (DETECT).

citations.quote: The application received a Complete Response on 06/25/2021 due to numerous product quality (PQ) and Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) deficiencies.

During the clinical site inspections for Study MW2010-03-02, a significant number of potential unblinding events were identified for assessments that were supposed to be conducted by blinded assessors.

During routine PDUFA and for-cause good clinical practice (GCP) inspections for Protocol MW2010-03-02, significant issues related to the conduct of the trial and GCP noncompliance were observed that impact the reliability of the eschar removal and wound closure assessments made by the first and second blinded assessors.
